data.body:
Fixes bug B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record: Seen 2026-10-23 recording D-recovery-one-design with --extends D-orphan-recovery: output 'added to D-orphan-recovery (decision, extends): no new record was made; globs added to it'. The new decision text was dropped and the old record's globs silently grew by ddflow/api/lifecycle/**. help says 'filed as a NEW record linked to ID'. Workaround: --new then 'ddflow link --extends'. Expected: a new record linked extends (as the help and the dedupe review's DX-decision-amend-relation imply), or a refusal that does not edit the old record.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record: decision add --extends ID appends to the old decision (adds its globs)...

data.claim: decision add --extends ID appends to ID (mutating it) whenever ID is still extendable, because `_dedupe._point` treats `extends` as an append for kinds outside LINK_ONLY_KINDS, which excludes decision.
data.falsifier: The probe returns a NEW record id D-new with an `extends` link to D-old and D-old's globs unchanged; or the probe shows D-old's globs grew with no D-new record.
data.mechanism: In _dedupe._point the append branch is `extendable(...) and (relation in (merge_into, duplicate_of) or tkind not in LINK_ONLY_KINDS)`; a decision has tkind='decision' (not in task/phase/research), so `extends` satisfies `tkind not in LINK_ONLY_KINDS` and calls `extend`, which appends text and unions globs onto D-old.
data.probe: python probe calling A.decision_add(D-old, globs='src/a.py') then A.decision_add(D-new, globs='src/a.py,src/b.py', answer=Answer('extends','D-old'))
data.probe_output: exit=0, data={id: D-old, extended: D-old, relation: extends, globs_added: [src/b.py]}; no D-new record, D-old globs unioned
data.question: Does `decision add --extends ID` currently append the new decision text to ID and union the new globs onto it (no new record), instead of filing a new decision linked to ID?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED probe: A.decision_add(D-old, globs='src/a.py') then A.decision_add(D-new, globs='src/a.py,src/b.py', answer=Answer('extends','D-old')) returned exit=0 data={id:'D-old',extended:'D-old',relation:'extends',globs_added:['src/b.py']} - no D-new record, D-old globs grew to ['src/a.py','src/b.py']. Cause: _dedupe._point appends for tkind not in LINK_ONLY_KINDS (task,phase,research), so a decision (extendable) is appended to instead of filing a new record. Research note R-fix-B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record CONFIRMED.

Ran ddflow brief --item fix-B-decision-extends-mutates-old-record. Relevant project rules: r-reuse-core (this fix reuses the existing _dedupe._point / extend machinery, changing only the constant and one condition; no new behaviour written twice); r-small-files (_dedupe.py stays ~478 lines, well under the 30KB split limit); r-no-shell (no shell dependency added). Governing decision D-no-deletion: 'A decision extension files a new record and never edits the old one'. Fix aligns decision with task/phase/research (LINK_ONLY_KINDS).

Committed 3ac17de51. Changed ddflow/api/_dedupe.py LINK_ONLY_KINDS to include 'decision' so `extends` files a new record linked to a decision (D-no-deletion) instead of appending; update _dedupe module docstring; rewrote decision-extends tests in tests/test_extend_globs.py (regression: test_decision_extends_files_a_new_linked_record_and_leaves_the_target) and added ddflow_decision_add to LINK_ONLY in tests/test_add_dedupe_mcp.py.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `LINK_ONLY` to include `ddflow_decision_add` while leaving `test_relation_merge_into_appends_to_the_target` parametrized over `LINK_ONLY` makes that existing test run for `ddflow_decision_add` and assert `merge_into:<old>` succeeds (`exit == 0`, `body["id"] == args["id"]`, `extended is None`). The newly added `test_relation_merge_into_a_decision_is_refused` exercises the same tool and relation and asserts `exit == 3` plus a refusal message. Therefore the test suite is internally inconsistent: if the implementation refuses decision `merge_into`, the old parametrized test fails on `exit == 0`; if it appends to the old decision, the new refusal test fails. The merge-into-append test should be parametrized over `APPENDS_ON_MERGE`, not `LINK_ONLY`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_add_dedupe_mcp.py:test_relation_merge_into_appends_to_the_target

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal message says `Answer extends:{chosen.target}`, but the answer format used/documented elsewhere in this module is `extends X` (space-separated). A user who follows this exact instruction after `merge_into D-orphan-recovery` will type `extends:D-orphan-recovery`, which the dedupe answer parser is not shown to accept; the suggested recovery is invalid. The refusal itself does not mutate the decision, so the fix works, but the corrective instruction is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:446

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only checks that `merge_into` returns exit code 3 and contains `"never edited in place"`; it never reads the old decision record after the call. An implementation that first appends the incoming globs to the old decision and then returns exactly that refusal would still pass this test. This fails to cover the intended “refusal that does not edit the old record” behavior, so the refusal path can still mutate the target decision without the regression test noticing.

evidence.note: Bug-hunted the change for off-by-one, empty-collection/vacuous-truth, silently-dropped config, torn-tail resume, unavailable-as-clean and dead knobs. No finding: extendable() decision branch is an unconditional return False; the merge_into decision refusal is a refused Outcome (no mutation writes); probes confirmed extends/duplicate_of file a new linked record and merge_into refuses, so no input drops the new decision text or mutates D-old. Regression test test_decision_extends_files_a_new_linked_record_and_leaves_the_target guards it.

No new duplicate code: the fix reuses the existing `extendable` / `_point` / `extend` machinery; the decision branch is one `return False` and one new refusal branch in `_point`, neither a duplicate of the existing merge_into/not-extendable refusal (that one lists claims/done/superseded, this one names D-no-deletion). No operation implemented twice.

chunk_findings.detail: The new decision guard refuses in-place mutation only when `chosen.relation == MERGE_INTO`, but the exact-copy extension path for `extends`/`duplicate_of` is still described by the changed module docstring as an extension (“... or the text is an exact copy of such a record”) and is not blocked by the new `extendable(..., "decision") == False` gate. Given an open/proposed `D-orphan-recovery`, a `decision add --extends D-orphan-recovery` (or a dedupe answer `duplicate_of:D-orphan-recovery`) whose decision text is an exact copy of the old decision but supplies a new glob such as `ddflow/api/lifecycle/**` can still return `extended=D-orphan-recovery`, so no new record is filed and the old decision’s globs grow. The added regression tests use different decision text (`SECOND`), so they do not catch this exact-copy mutation path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:_point

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test checks that the target decision's globs are unchanged, but it does not check that the target decision's text/title are unchanged. For the input seeded by `seed_decision(repo, "src/a.py")` followed by `decision add` with `id="D-new"`, `title=SECOND`, `decision=SECOND`, `globs=["src/b.py"]`, `extends="D-old"`, the test passes even if the implementation files `D-new` correctly but also overwrites `D-old.decision` (or `D-old.title`) with `SECOND` while leaving `D-old.globs == ["src/a.py"]`. Since the stated invariant is that a decision is never edited in place, this assertion gap lets a fix that still mutates the old decision's text pass the regression test.
